qbank.name: Clinical Basics · Sample Qbank
qbank.description: Ten starter questions covering high-yield clinical basics. Delete anytime.

questions.title: Anaphylaxis
questions.question: A 24-year-old develops urticaria, stridor and hypotension minutes after a peanut exposure. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.explanation: IM adrenaline (epinephrine) into the anterolateral thigh is first-line in anaphylaxis — adult dose 0.5 mg of 1:1000. Antihistamines and steroids are adjuncts and never replace adrenaline. Repeat every 5 minutes if needed.

questions.title: Inferior MI
questions.question: ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF indicates infarction of which territory, usually supplied by which artery?
questions.explanation: II, III and aVF look at the inferior wall, supplied by the right coronary artery in ~80% of people. Check for reciprocal depression in I/aVL and consider right ventricular involvement (V4R).

questions.title: Normal potassium
questions.question: Which is the normal adult serum potassium range?
questions.explanation: Normal serum K⁺ is 3.5–5.0 mmol/L. Below 3.5 → hypokalaemia (flat T waves, U waves); above 5.0 → hyperkalaemia (peaked T waves, widening QRS).

questions.title: Cranial nerve II
questions.question: Which cranial nerve carries vision?
questions.explanation: CN II (optic) is purely sensory for vision and the afferent limb of the pupillary light reflex. CN III, IV and VI move the eye; CN V is facial sensation.

questions.title: DKA first step
questions.question: A patient presents with glucose 28 mmol/L, ketones 4 mmol/L and pH 7.15. What is the most appropriate initial step?
questions.explanation: In DKA, start with IV 0.9% saline — patients are profoundly volume-depleted. Fixed-rate insulin follows; add potassium to fluids once K⁺ < 5.5 and urine output is established. Bicarbonate is not routine.

questions.title: CAP organism
questions.question: What is the most common cause of community-acquired pneumonia?
questions.explanation: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains the commonest CAP pathogen worldwide. Atypicals (Mycoplasma, Legionella) and viruses follow; consider severity scores (CURB-65) to guide site of care.

questions.title: Warfarin monitoring
questions.question: Which test monitors warfarin therapy?
questions.explanation: Warfarin is monitored with the INR (standardised prothrombin time). Heparin uses APTT (or anti-Xa for LMWH); DOACs need no routine monitoring.

questions.title: Acute asthma
questions.question: First-line treatment of an acute severe asthma exacerbation includes oxygen plus which inhaled drug?
questions.explanation: Salbutamol (SABA), nebulised or via spacer, is first-line, driven by oxygen; add ipratropium in severe cases, plus systemic steroids early. Target SpO₂ 94–98%.

questions.title: LV failure
questions.question: Left ventricular failure most characteristically produces which finding?
questions.explanation: LV failure backs pressure into the pulmonary circulation → pulmonary oedema: dyspnoea, orthopnoea, PND, bibasal crackles. Peripheral oedema and raised JVP are right-sided features.

questions.title: Hyperkalaemia ECG
questions.question: Which ECG features are typical of hyperkalaemia? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Hyperkalaemia causes tall peaked T waves and progressive QRS widening (also PR prolongation, loss of P waves, sine-wave pattern). Prominent U waves and flattened T waves belong to hypokalaemia.

cards.name: Normal Values · Sample Cards
cards.description: Twelve essential normal ranges as flip cards.

cards.title: Respiratory rate
cards.back:
12–20 breaths/min

RR is the most sensitive early vital sign of deterioration.

cards.title: SpO₂
cards.back:
95–100%

Target 88–92% in patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure.

cards.title: Creatinine
cards.back:
~0.6–1.2 mg/dL (53–106 µmol/L)

Interpret with muscle mass and trend, not a single value.

library.name: MedGURU Guide
library.description: How to use every feature, plus the science of studying well.

docs.title: Welcome to MedGURU
docs.html:
MedGURU is an offline study app made by Dr Sarwar Alam. It reads the study packs you already own and turns them into question sessions, flashcards and a reference library.

The three pack types

  • Qbanks — timed-style question sessions with explanations and progress.
  • Flashcards — decks you flip through and grade.
  • Libraries — article collections with a table of contents and full-text search.

Your data stays yours

No account. No cloud. No tracking. The app has no internet permission — it works in airplane mode forever. Progress lives in a private database on this device.

Delete these sample packs anytime from Packs → ⋯ → Delete. Your progress is kept if you ever re-import them.

docs.title: Importing your packs
docs.html:
The ZIP format

Each pack is a ZIP containing one top-level folder:

  • a SQLite database (.db, .sqlite, .sqlite3 or .bin)
  • optionally manifest.json (name, type, publisher) and icon.png
  • optionally a media/ or Images/ folder

How to import

  1. Open Packs.
  2. Tap Import ZIP and pick the file.
  3. Wait for extraction — the pack appears in the list, ready to study.

Qbanks, flashcards and article libraries are detected automatically, with or without a manifest. Re-importing an updated pack replaces its files but keeps your progress.

Not supported yet

Lexi-Drugs, VisualDX and Access-Medicine packs use different schemas and are rejected with a clear message.

docs.title: Question bank sessions
docs.html:
Building a session

Filter by subject and system, choose a question count, and pick a status:

  • Unseen — questions you have never answered.
  • Missed — questions you got wrong, for a second pass.
  • Flagged — questions you marked with the flag icon.

Answering

Tap an option, then Submit. Some questions accept multiple answers — a chip tells you when. After submitting you get the explanation, the option distribution, and references.

Never lose a session

Leaving mid-session saves everything. Resume from the pack screen or the Study tab. At the end, review every question or tap Retry missed to drill only your errors.

docs.title: Flashcards
docs.html:
Flip and grade

Tap a card to reveal the back. Then grade yourself:

  • Got it (or swipe right) — marks the card known and moves on.
  • Again (or swipe left) — sends the card to the end of the queue so you see it once more this run.

Known cards persist between sessions, and each deck shows a progress ring. Use shuffle to break order effects — recalling a card in a new sequence is stronger practice.

Honest grading beats fast grading. If you hesitated, press Again.

docs.title: Library & search
docs.html:
Browsing

Libraries open as a table of contents: folders expand, articles open in a clean reading view. Use the arrows at the end of an article to move to the next one in the same section.

Reading comfort

The Aa menu adjusts text size, switches to a serif reading font, and changes the page theme (Night, Paper, OLED). Bookmarks are one tap away in the top bar.

Search

The search box scans the whole library — titles and full text — and highlights your term in the results. Images in articles can be tapped to open a zoomable viewer.

docs.title: Study smarter
docs.html:
What actually works

Decades of learning research converge on a few techniques:

  • Active recall — retrieving an answer beats re-reading it. Questions and flashcards are recall machines; use them before you feel ready.
  • Spaced repetition — revisit material across days, not in one block. The Missed filter is your spacing tool: re-drill errors tomorrow, then next week.
  • Interleaving — mix subjects and systems (Random order) rather than blocking one topic. It feels harder and produces better transfer.
  • The testing effect — being tested on material improves later retention more than extra study time, even without feedback.

A simple daily loop

  1. Quick 10 unseen questions to start the day.
  2. Read the library article for whatever you missed.
  3. Flip the matching flashcard deck.
  4. Finish with Retry missed on yesterday's errors.

Normal values at a glance

Sodium135–145 mmol/L
Potassium3.5–5.0 mmol/L
WBC4–11 × 10⁹/L
Platelets150–400 × 10⁹/L
Fasting glucose70–99 mg/dL

Sample content for demonstration — always confirm against your primary references.
